text: The UAE does not recognise EU or EEA status and gives it no advantage. The categories that exist are UAE national, resident and international, and a Danish student is in the last. See the non-EU row.

Birmingham Dubai sets a separate, harder deadline for new international students to apply for a University-sponsored visa from outside the UAE — 24 August 2026 for the September 2026 intake. For an applicant living in Denmark this, not the application, is the binding date, and the 2027 one is not yet published.

Rarely mentioned to foreigners: a federal network of seven colleges across Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Al Dhafra, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, awarding applied diplomas and bachelor's degrees across around forty programmes. It is the UAE's nearest equivalent to a Danish erhvervsakademi — shorter, vocational, employer-facing — and it rarely appears in English-language guides to studying in the Gulf.

The UAE is socially conservative by Danish standards. Laws on alcohol, relationships outside marriage and public behaviour differ from what you are used to, and enforcement varies by emirate. Read the Danish foreign ministry's travel advice properly, not the marketing brochures.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before budgeting.

There is no EU or EEA fee category in Australia and no reciprocal arrangement with Denmark. Commonwealth Supported Places, the subsidised domestic rate, are for Australian and New Zealand citizens and permanent residents. A Danish student pays the full international fee.

The IB Diploma is converted to a Combined Rank, an ATAR-like value, on a schedule determined nationally by the Australasian Conference of Tertiary Admissions Centres and re-set every February. Two schedules are published on one page: one converting a fine-grained IB Admissions Score in quarter-point steps, which applies only to candidates who sat the IB in Australia from November 2022; and the one recorded here, which converts the whole diploma score and applies to everyone else, including a candidate sitting the May session in Denmark.

The one part of Australia where a Danish IB candidate is confirmed to be inside a shared admissions system. UAC takes international applicants holding an International Baccalaureate Diploma, with no condition about where it was sat, and one application and one charge cover every participating institution preferenced. Applying directly to the university is also available here; UAC is an alternative rather than an obligation.

UWA, Curtin and the other Western Australian universities. The admissions centre here draws its line on citizenship rather than on where the exams were sat, which excludes a Danish applicant however the IB was taken.
Danish SU may in some circumstances support a full degree abroad. Check su.dk and ask your studievejleder well before you apply.

Australia is declared as dividing by jurisdiction because the division is real for our reader and only for our reader: the IB conversion is national and identical everywhere, and what differs by state is whether the shared admissions system will accept an application from someone sitting the exams in Denmark. In four of the five jurisdictions the answer is no or unknown, which is why four of them route to the same direct application - that is a finding, not a tidy default.

Australia's entry rules are easy to read. The International Baccalaureate is not merely accepted here; it is converted, on a published national schedule agreed by all the state admissions centres, into an ATAR-like Combined Rank, and universities state the rank each degree needs. That means a Danish student can work out in an afternoon whether they are in range. Everything else about it is harder. The academic year runs from late February, so finishing the IB in May 2027 leads either to a July 2027 mid-year start, which many degrees do not offer, or to February 2028. Applying is institution-by-institution almost everywhere. And the student visa carries a real financial test that has to be satisfied on top of full international tuition.

Two conversion tables sit on one UAC page and the wrong one looks more authoritative. The quarter-point IB Admissions Score schedule is only for candidates who sat the IB in Australia; a Danish candidate is converted from the whole diploma score.
Three-year bachelor's degrees, so you finish in the same time as in Denmark, with a fourth honours year only if you choose it.

Canada has no EU or EEA fee category. The line is drawn at Canadian citizenship or permanent residence, so a Danish student pays the full international rate everywhere, with no reciprocal arrangement of any kind.

Quebec bachelor's degrees are often three years rather than four because Quebec students arrive having done two years of CEGEP. An IB Diploma holder from abroad enters the university directly and takes the longer version. Confirm the programme length before accepting.

Continuous health and hospitalisation insurance for the entire study stay is a condition of the CAQ, not merely a requirement on arrival. Whether a Danish student can instead join the Quebec public plan through a social security agreement is not confirmed here; ask the RAMQ or your university.
Danish SU may in some circumstances support a full degree abroad. Check su.dk and talk to your studievejleder early.

Provincial, not national, and very different from one province to the next. Ontario excludes international students from the public plan entirely and enrols them in UHIP; British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia admit them on their own conditions, each after a wait; Quebec requires continuous private or public cover for the whole study stay as a condition of the CAQ. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid anywhere in Canada.

Most universities guarantee first-year residence only to students who apply by a separate housing deadline, months before term and usually in spring. UBC's is 1 May 2027. Take the guarantee: Vancouver and Toronto private rentals are very expensive and finding a room from Denmark is very hard.

Not established: whether a Danish student qualifies for the Quebec public health plan under a social security agreement, because the RAMQ pages are behind a bot-protection challenge; the length of Nova Scotia's health-cover waiting period; and what any Canadian college or CEGEP requires of an IB Diploma holder.

In Quebec a bachelor's is often three years, because a Quebec student has already spent two years at CEGEP. An IB Diploma holder arriving from abroad takes the longer version. Confirm the length before accepting an offer.

Certificates, diplomas, apprenticeships and some degrees, taught for a named occupation rather than a discipline. Ontario alone has 24 of them, and they are applied for through ontariocolleges.ca rather than the OUAC - a different central service for a different sector in the same province. Admission is stated in terms of an Ontario high school diploma, and what that means for an IB Diploma holder from abroad is not published; Ontario's answer is to contact a college directly.

It is rarely mentioned to students from abroad, and it is the reason Quebec degrees look short. What it would mean for an IB Diploma holder is not known: whether a full Diploma is treated as over-qualification for a pre-university DEC, and whether a technical DEC would admit one, are open questions to put to the Fédération des cégeps.
At ETH Zurich, CHF 2,190 per semester for students coming from abroad; CHF 730 for Swiss residents. Other universities set their own fees.
Fees depend on residence, not EU citizenship: at ETH a student from Denmark pays the foreign rate.

China is two systems for a Danish IB student. The Sino-foreign joint universities, such as NYU Shanghai, Duke Kunshan and XJTLU, teach in English and admit on their own or the American calendar. The Chinese universities, such as Tsinghua, Peking and Zhejiang, admit international students through their own application-and-review process. Since 2026/2027 that process requires a new national test, the CSCA, and most of their programmes are taught in Chinese.
DKK
Tuition is charged, plus a DKK 3,060 residence permit fee and proof of DKK 7,426 per month of self-support.

HL generally becomes Danish A level and SL becomes B level. Both post-2019 mathematics courses count identically: Analysis and Approaches HL and Applications and Interpretation HL are both Mathematics A; both SL courses are Mathematics B. Global Politics has no fixed equivalence and is assessed institution by institution.
For Danish-taught programmes you need Danish at A level. Danish A1 or Danish A Literature at either level satisfies it; Danish A1 SL sits above the Studieprøven test and is normally accepted.
If you took Danish B HL or Danish ab initio, whether it substitutes for Danish A is decided by each institution. Ask in writing.
SU, the state education grant: DKK 7,426 per month before tax in 2026 for a student living away from home, with a loan of up to DKK 3,799 on top.
Non-Danish EU citizens must first obtain equal-treatment status, in practice by working 10–12 hours a week for at least ten continuous weeks and continuing while receiving SU.
Students on a non-EU study residence permit may not claim SU or housing benefit, and doing so can cost them the permit.

Once you have a CPR number you receive a health card automatically and healthcare is free. Choose insurance group 1, as 98% of residents do: an assigned GP, free consultations, referrals to specialists. Dental care and physiotherapy are not covered.
Midpoint of the official DKK 8,450–13,700 range. Copenhagen sits at the top of it; Esbjerg, Sønderborg and Aalborg well below.

EU and EEA citizens apply to SIRI for an EU registration certificate within three months of arriving, bringing a passport and letter of admission. Then a CPR number from your municipality, then a health card, then a bank account and NemKonto — each step depends on the one before it.
The SU reform taking effect on 1 January 2027 cuts the grant frame for higher education from 70 to 58 portions and limits SU to the prescribed length of your programme.
Applicants without MitID must print the signature page, sign it by hand and send it to every institution by 15 March, 12:00. It is never uploaded, and the application is incomplete without it.
No tuition at all for EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, and SU on top if you are a Danish citizen.
Almost always restricted to UK residents, so rarely open to an applicant from Denmark. Recorded so that the restriction is visible rather than discovered late.
Apply to the college. Degrees are validated or accredited abroad.

Greek public universities teach almost entirely in Greek. There are two ways in for a Danish IB student. The first is one of about twenty English-taught bachelor's at public universities, applied for directly on the IB, which charge €4,500–€17,000 a year. The second is a Greek-taught place through the ministry's eight-day July window for graduates of foreign schools, which needs B2 Greek before you can enrol. Private colleges such as ACG teach in English and award US- or UK-validated degrees.
Hong Kong has no EU category. A Danish student is non-local and pays the non-local fee.

Hong Kong's universities teach in English and read the IB directly. A Danish student is a non-local applicant: you apply to each university on its own site, not through JUPAS. The early rounds close in November 2026, on predicted grades. Fees are high, about HK$250,000 to 280,000 a year at HKU.
Not established: whether any felsőoktatási szakképzés is taught in English, or open to an IB applicant from abroad.

Ireland reorganised its sector recently and the vocabulary has not caught up: most of the institutes of technology have merged into Technological Universities, so guidance written a few years ago describes institutions that no longer exist under those names. Underneath that, the structure is a familiar one — universities, technological universities, specialist colleges and further education, with the last of these far more useful to an international applicant than it first appears.

MEXT's scholarship route applies its own academic condition, but the Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer the undergraduate scholarship to Danish nationals, so it is not a route for this cohort.

MEXT Undergraduate Scholarship, Embassy Recommendation: in the 2027 round, five years including a preparatory year in Japanese, 117,000 yen a month, fees waived and air tickets paid, with MEXT choosing the university. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer this type to Danish nationals, so it is listed only because people ask about it.
Danish SU follows separate rules for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before assuming it travels with you.

Enrolment in National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70 per cent of medical costs and students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. A Danish EHIC does not apply.

Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise a first-year place in a university dormitory or international house, which is cheaper and far simpler than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's pages refuse plain fetches (HTTP 403) but open in an ordinary browser; the Study in Japan page was read that way on 2026-09-24.

The MEXT undergraduate scholarship is not open to you from Denmark. The Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen lists two MEXT types for Danish nationals — Japanese Studies and Research Student, both for students already at university. Plan around institutional awards, and ask the embassy in writing if MEXT matters to you.

The route an IB student from a Danish gymnasium uses is the twelve-years-abroad category, not the general foreigner category, and the two have different documentary requirements at several universities.

The Global Korea Scholarship, on the University Track only for a Danish citizen. In the 2027 round it covered tuition up to 5m KRW a semester, a Korean language year, airfare and 14.4m KRW a year during the degree, over five to seven years. Its Embassy Track invites 74 countries and Denmark is not one.

International students staying more than six months are enrolled in the National Health Insurance Service and pay a monthly premium — KAIST puts it at 458,340 KRW a semester. It is compulsory, and Korean healthcare is fast and inexpensive at the point of use. A Danish EHIC does not apply.

University dormitories are the standard and by far the easiest route for a first-year international student: cheap, on campus, and usually allocated with the admission. KAIST publishes 664,000 KRW a semester for a place. The private Seoul market needs a large jeonse or wolse deposit that is impractical to raise from Denmark, so apply for the dormitory the moment an offer arrives.

The route everything else is described against. Four years to a bachelor's degree, six for medicine, Korean medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine. Admission for an applicant schooled entirely abroad runs through a separate international track with its own rounds, its own documents and no Suneung. This is where every English-taught undergraduate programme named on this page sits.

Korea's Ministry of Education divides higher education into more kinds than English-language guides usually show. Alongside the four-year 대학교 that every foreigner has heard of sit 전문대학 junior colleges, national 교육대학 for primary teachers, the special-law science and technology institutes, polytechnic colleges under the labour ministry rather than this one, and open and cyber universities. An IB Diploma opens the first three of those; the junior college is rarely mentioned to foreigners and is the nearest Korean relative of the Danish erhvervsakademi.

Korea keeps a separate admissions track for applicants who did all twelve years of school abroad, and an IB Diploma fits it: no Suneung, a small international pool, and a decision on transcript, essays and often an interview. The catch is the calendar. The Korean year begins in March, and March 2027 is out of reach for a May 2027 candidate, so the real choices are September 2027 on predicted grades or March 2028 with results. English-taught degrees are concentrated at Yonsei's Underwood International College, KAIST, POSTECH, UNIST and GIST, plus specific divisions elsewhere.

The Global Korea Scholarship's Embassy Track is closed to Danish citizens — 74 countries are invited for 2027 and Denmark is not one of them. Only the University Track's UIC Program is open, and it is science and engineering at thirteen named universities, none of them the ones above.

Removed from the institution list on 2026-09-24: the Miami University Dolibois European Center (MUDEC). It is a study-abroad campus for Miami University students, not a place a school leaver can apply to for a degree.
The only public university. Three-year bachelor's degrees, often bilingual, with a compulsory semester abroad. Eligibility depends on your nationality, residence and where your diploma is from.

Luxembourg has one public university, founded in 2003, where many bachelor's degrees are taught in two languages and every bachelor student spends a semester abroad. There is one intake a year, in September, and applications for 2027 open on 1 February 2027. Language, not points, is what decides whether a programme is open to you.
One multilingual university, and a compulsory semester abroad
Sacred Heart University's Luxembourg campus and the BBI hospitality school, still listed on many study-abroad sites, are not options: one closed and the other's website no longer exists.
A semester abroad is built into every bachelor's degree.
Not established: whether an EU citizen from Denmark can compete for Latvian state-funded (budget) places on an English-taught programme; whether institutions admit on predicted IB grades.
The general requirement includes SEC Maltese. If you were educated abroad you may offer another language instead, with Admissions Board approval.

A build check in src/lib/data.mjs treats every canonical institution as Danish and compares its id against the image keys derived from countries/nl.json. Canonical ids nl-um, nl-eur and nl-buas collided with the country profile's own entries for the same three universities and failed the build with 'one of them would show the other's photograph' — a false positive, since they are the same institutions. Since data/countries/nl.json was out of scope, the canonical ids were renamed to nl-maastricht, nl-erasmus and nl-breda-uas instead. The check is still wrong and will catch the next Destination that migrates.

What works end to end, checked rather than assumed: all sixteen Dutch Opportunities are assessed in /planner/ against a Danish IB profile — thirteen meet, Nanobiology is Possible with action for want of Biology HL, Technical Computer Science is Needs review for the reason above. The engine's sentence reads 'Your Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL meets HL. This requirement is published in IB terms, so nothing is converted.' That is ADR 0002 working as designed on a Destination with no Recognition Scheme, which is the test the ADR said had to pass.

MODEL FRICTION, all of it in src/ and none of it worked around in the data. (1) src/lib/canonical.mjs denormalise() understands only kind 'local-equivalency', so a requirement written in IB terms projects to entryRequirements: null and a Dutch programme page renders the heading 'And one of these combinations' above an empty list. ADR 0002 added the ib-subject path to the schema and to the engine; this projection into the page templates was not updated with it. (2) The same projection builds extraRequirements from the requirement kinds essay/test/portfolio/interview/audition/other without consulting `mandatory`, so a Selection Factor renders on the programme page under 'On top of the subjects' as though it were an entry requirement. On the Erasmus IBA page a student sees 'Your grade average — 75 per cent of the selection score' in the same list as things they must hold. The answer to 'can a student tell a Requirement from a Selection Factor on the page' is currently no. (3) assess() returns selection.factors and nothing renders it; admission.capacityNote is not rendered anywhere, so numerus fixus capacity and the hard 15 January date reach a page only through an Application Route milestone. (4) The restricted-admission note on a programme page is Danish copy — it talks about quota cut-offs and national intake policy — and it now appears on Dutch pages. (5) src/pages/programmes.mjs describes the planner as checking 'every English-taught programme in Denmark' and converting subjects 'using the Danish Agency's official table'; it now also checks sixteen Dutch ones and converts nothing for them.

The Netherlands is a common choice for a Danish IB student who wants an English-taught degree in Europe: hundreds of bachelor programmes taught entirely in English, three-year research-university degrees, a low statutory fee, and an application process that runs through one portal. All of that is still true and the first part of it is contracting, because a law now going through requires bachelor programmes to be taught mainly in Dutch unless the institution can justify otherwise. Universities have already begun converting and capping English tracks.
There is no national IB-to-Dutch grade conversion. If you are coming from the Danish system, do not go looking for one.

Norwegian-taught programmes require documented Norwegian. For an IB applicant, Danish A (higher or standard level) at grade 3 or better documents it; without Danish A you need an approved Norwegian test.

Norway merged most of its colleges into its universities over the last decade, so the sector looks flatter than the Danish or Dutch one: a smaller number of large, multi-campus universities, alongside specialist institutions and a set of private providers that matter more here than the word "private" suggests elsewhere.

Norway charges EEA students no tuition and sits an hour from Copenhagen. The obstacle is language: Norwegian higher education is taught in Norwegian, several of the largest universities offer no English-taught bachelor programme at all, and the English-taught set nationally is small enough to list. For a Danish IB student that obstacle is lower than it looks: the national admissions service counts Danish A at grade 3 or better as documented Norwegian.
Free, close to home, and almost entirely in Norwegian
Danish A at grade 3 or better meets the Norwegian language requirement for general admission, so the whole Norwegian-taught system is formally open to a Danish IB student.
Nordic mobility arrangements are well established, and for a Danish student SU treats Nordic study more generously than the rest.
New Zealand has no EU or EEA fee category and no arrangement with Denmark. A Danish student pays the international fee, set by each university.
Danish SU may in some circumstances follow you abroad for a full degree. Check su.dk and speak to your studievejleder early.

International students on a student visa are generally not entitled to publicly funded healthcare, so Immigration New Zealand requires insurance acceptable to your education provider for the whole period of study, and universities normally sell or arrange a compliant policy. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid. Budget for it as a separate annual cost.

First-year students are strongly steered into halls of residence and most universities guarantee a place if you apply by their deadline. Take it: renting privately from Denmark is difficult, and the halls are where the year's friendships are made. Otago is famous for an almost entirely residential first year in Dunedin. Auckland and Wellington rents are high; Dunedin, Hamilton, Palmerston North and Christchurch are much cheaper.
Studying medicine here to practise in Denmark involves more than the diploma — read the medicine-abroad page before committing.

A Nordic institution with no equivalent in most systems: a year or more of non-degree study, often residential, sometimes to fill a qualification gap and sometimes simply to work out what you want. It is not higher education and it is not a waste of a year, and it is one reason a Swedish or Danish student taking time out is not doing the same thing as a British student on a gap year.

Sweden divides its institutions by research rights rather than by vocation, which is a different cut from the Danish or Dutch one and catches people out. A universitet may award doctorates across the board; a högskola is a university college that may not, or may only in named areas — but it teaches bachelor degrees of the same standing, and several are highly regarded. Alongside both sit the specialist arts institutions and, distinctively Nordic, the folkhögskola.
For a Danish student the practical distance is small and Nordic mobility is well established.
Singapore does not recognise EU or EEA status. Its categories are Singapore Citizen, Singapore Permanent Resident and International Student, and a Danish student is the third. See the non-EU row.

Programme-specific Higher Level requirements apply — engineering and computing normally want HL Mathematics, medicine HL Chemistry and Biology — so check each programme. A different kind of rule matters too: NTU excludes a May-session IB candidate from Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, and Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education) entirely, because those programmes decide before IB results exist. That is a subject restriction imposed by the calendar rather than by the syllabus, and it can catch a Danish applicant.

Audited 2026-09-24 (docs/research/audit/sg.md). Not established: SUSS's 2027 dates, because its admissions pages sit behind a bot-detection challenge this project does not complete — that is our gap, not theirs; SMU's, SUTD's, SIT's and NAFA's 2027 dates, which those institutions have not yet published; AY2027/2028 tuition anywhere, and tuition at SMU and SUTD; indicative IB grade profiles anywhere; whether the Tuition Grant reaches an international student at LASALLE, NAFA or any private institution; and what the polytechnic route offers an IB holder from abroad.

Not covered here. Whether an IB Diploma holder from abroad can enrol, what it costs and whether the Tuition Grant applies are all open questions. Listed because the route exists, is large, and explains why SIT's admissions calendar is built around polytechnic results rather than IB ones.

Five polytechnics — Singapore, Ngee Ann, Temasek, Nanyang and Republic — awarding three-year applied diplomas that are the ordinary post-secondary destination for a large share of Singaporeans, and a recognised route onward into the Autonomous Universities with advanced standing. This is Singapore's answer to the Danish erhvervsakademi and it is rarely described to a foreign applicant.

Actual results are due at NTU within three days of release — the first week of July, in the middle of the Danish summer. The IBO transcript authorisation that makes that possible must be arranged before July, and an application without it gets no outcome at all. NUS requires the same authorisation from every IB applicant (institute code 000690).
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk early.

The University of Ljubljana says an IB Diploma is equivalent to the Slovenian matura and needs no recognition procedure, while IB certificates without the Diploma do. The national Study in Slovenia portal says anyone schooled abroad must obtain a recognition decision, and names no exemption. Ask the faculty before relying on either.
The University of Ljubljana's one English bachelor's (Business and Economics) was open only in the non-EU rounds and to Slovenes abroad in the 2026/2027 call.
Not established: whether any higher vocational college teaches in English or admits an IB applicant from abroad; the art academies' language of teaching.
The 2027/28 dates come from a joint call not yet published. The first round is decided in late July and enrolment follows in August — during the Danish summer holiday.

At a public university a Danish student pays the non-resident rate for all four years, because residency for tuition is not something an F-1 student acquires by living in the state. The University of California publishes both figures for 2027–28: UC Tuition of 16,278 USD for a California resident and 57,300 USD for a nonresident, with a total on-campus cost of attendance of 49,078 and 90,100 USD. UC also holds its tuition line flat for up to six years under a Tuition Stability Plan. The other public universities here publish 2026–27 figures: Michigan charges non-residents 67,096 USD in tuition and fees in the first two years of LSA (total budget 88,394 USD), Illinois quotes 42,248–53,078 USD for international students (total 62,146–72,976 USD), and Arizona State puts an international student's total at 69,906 USD.

This group mixes private colleges, where there is a single published price for everyone and the question is how much aid discounts it — Harvard's 2026–27 billed cost is 91,634 USD — with three public universities, Michigan, Illinois and Arizona State, where a Danish student pays a non-resident or international rate for all four years: 67,096 USD in tuition and fees at Michigan (first two years of LSA), 42,248–53,078 USD at Illinois and up to 42,609 USD at Arizona State for 2026–27. Application fees also vary inside the group from nothing at Colby to 100 USD at Stanford.

For 2027–28 UC publishes UC Tuition of 16,278 USD for a California resident and 57,300 USD for a nonresident, a gap of a little over 41,000 USD a year, with total on-campus costs of 49,078 and 90,100 USD. A Danish student is a nonresident and stays one — residency for tuition is not something an F-1 student acquires by living in California. The one piece of good news is the Tuition Stability Plan, which holds the tuition line flat for up to six years.

Compulsory, expensive, and charged to the bill automatically rather than offered. Every registered UC Berkeley student, international students included, is enrolled in the campus plan at 2,533 USD per semester for undergraduates in 2026–27 unless they waive it with proof of comparable cover. In Massachusetts it is state law: Harvard states that Massachusetts law requires any full-time or part-time student at an institution of higher learning in the state to hold qualifying student health insurance or comparable cover, and its waiver closes on 31 July. A Danish travel or study policy may be comprehensive and still fail, because a waiver also requires the cover to be reasonably accessible where you are living.

Not established: whether an F-1 student from Denmark can hold a University of California Transfer Admission Guarantee on the same terms as a California resident. This is the question the community-college route turns on and the per-campus TAG matrix was not opened.

Owned by a state and built to educate its residents — Michigan, Illinois, Berkeley, Arizona State. Large, strong in engineering and the sciences, and priced in two tiers: a resident rate and a non-resident rate that a Danish student pays for all four years. Institutional aid for international students is limited or absent; Michigan states that international students on temporary visas should expect to pay the full cost of attendance. These are also the institutions where the application route is least predictable, because some are on the Common App and some are on their own state system.

A cheap route into an American degree, and a rarely mentioned one. One gap: whether an F-1 student from Denmark can hold a Transfer Admission Guarantee on the same terms as a Californian resident is not established here, and nobody should plan around it until it is.

Early Decision is a contract, not a preference. Amherst's wording is that you agree not to be an Early Decision candidate anywhere else and, if admitted, to withdraw your applications from other colleges and enrol. It raises your odds and it ends your ability to compare financial aid offers, which for a family paying from Denmark is usually the more expensive loss.

Health insurance is compulsory, expensive and charged automatically. Every registered Berkeley student including international students is enrolled in the campus plan unless they waive it; in Massachusetts it is state law. A Danish policy may be comprehensive and still fail the waiver because it is not accessible where you are living.
